title: Tensor products of globally generated invertible sheaves are globally generated
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $n\ge 1$ be an integer, and let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_n$ be globally generated invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Use the left-associated product and induced pure tensor sections [def-sc-positive-tensor-family]. Then the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] $\mathcal L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\cdots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$ is a globally generated invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, Each factor admits a finite global generating family, and for every choice of such finite generating families, their pure tensor sections generate the tensor product.

proof.text: Induct on n. The zero case is hL 0; the successor uses the proven source-library instance IsInvertible.tensorObj in ProjectionFormula, the tensor-invertibility part of lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible, on the induction hypothesis and the last factor.

For each factor apply lem-sc-finite-global-generating-family and choose its finite generating family. Apply lem-sc-finite-tensor-generating-sections to this family, construct a GeneratingSections record from its tuple-indexed epi, and retain the universal version of the same lemma for all finite generating families. Combine these with the invertibility induction to prove all four conjuncts.

statement_change.old_statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $n\ge 1$ be an integer, and let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_n$ be globally generated invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Then the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] $\mathcal L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\cdots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$ is a globally generated invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, generated by the tensor products of finite global generating families of the factors.
statement_change.what: Global generation on an arbitrary non-quasi-compact scheme does not imply existence of finite global generating families. For example take the disjoint union of projective spaces P^d over a field for all d >= 1, with O(1) on each component: it is globally generated, but r global sections cannot generate O(1) on P^d when d >= r (their common linear zero locus is nonempty). The source 09NC assumes quasi-compactness throughout, and uses it to choose finite families. Restored that source hypothesis and made the finite-family assertion explicit. Added the definition of the left-associated product and its sections, without changing the blueprint unit statement.

old_proof.text: By induction on $n$, the tensor product $\mathcal L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\cdots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$ is invertible. Here the $n$-fold tensor product is the iterated one, $\mathcal L_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_n=(\mathcal L_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_{n-1})\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $n=1$ there is nothing to prove; for $n\ge 2$ the first factor is invertible by induction and the tensor product of two invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1).

Choose finite global generating families for each $\mathcal L_i$, as supplied by global generation. The tensor products of these sections generate the tensor product module by [lem-sc-tensor-generating-sections]. Hence the tensor product is globally generated, and the displayed tensor products are a generating family.
